BAM Seek

Variant evidence across current and historical samples.

Local processing · no uploads · no runtime network requests

BAM sources

Select coordinate-sorted BAMs together with their BAI or CSI indexes. Select a radio button to designate the current sample; all others are historical.

One-based genomic coordinates and REF/ALT required. Accepts genomic HGVS, VCF columns, annotated genomic variants and report rows. Small indels require a shared left anchor. Equivalent shifted indels are not normalized.

The fixed hg19 disease panel is always included.

Calculation settings and IGV reference

A reference is needed only for IGV sequence/mismatch display. Choose the same reference assembly as the BAM. IGV windows use first-of-pair strand colors, paired display, base sorting, and no downsampling. Windows are temporary; reopen them from a result after a reload.

Select indexed BAMs to begin.

Variant evidence

Disease panel

Fixed hg19 hotspots; repeated sites are calculated once per BAM. TP53 whole-gene review remains pipeline-managed.

Phasing findings

Direct molecular linkage only. AB = ALT/ALT, Ab = ALT/REF, aB = REF/ALT, ab = REF/REF. Unsequenced insert gaps do not establish linkage.

Dev local phasing (experimental)

Rare markers support cis through repeated positive co-occurrence. Common markers may support trans through opposite haplotypes. Marker absence and target REF alone carry no phase meaning.

Comparison narrative

Draft wording assumes the Current and Historical variant boxes contain reported calls from the same patient. Review the wording against assay thresholds, coverage and the displayed evidence before use. Variants in Both boxes are excluded.

All numeric evidence
For research use only. Files, settings and caches stay in memory and are discarded on reload.

About BAM Seek

Use

Select coordinate-sorted BAM files and their matching BAI or CSI indexes. Designate at most one current sample, choose the alignment assembly, and enter current and historical variants with genomic coordinates and REF/ALT. The fixed hg19 disease panel runs alongside the entered variants.

Evidence and phase

Read VAF uses ALT/(ALT+REF). Molecule VAF uses independent read-name fragments or the selected MI/RX/UB grouping. OTHER calls and ambiguous molecules are excluded from the denominators. Direct phasing requires actual observations of both sites. Experimental local phasing uses repeated rare-marker co-occurrence for cis and opposite common-marker haplotypes for trans.

IGV review

Select a local 2bit reference or uncompressed FASTA with FAI. Each result opens a temporary igv.js window with paired alignments, first-of-pair strand coloring, base sorting at the variant and sampling disabled. Files are read locally and the bundled viewer requires no network. Wide views may require zooming in. Reloading a temporary window requires reopening it from the results.

Privacy and interpretation

Files, settings and caches are held in memory. External resource links open only when selected and contain structured variant identifiers. Review draft narratives against assay thresholds and coverage before use. No desktop command relay is required.

For research use only.
